name: ε Eridani
description: K dwarf 3.2 parsecs away, 5,039 K, with a Jupiter-mass planet.

radius.source: Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: the Navy Optical Interferometer limb-darkened angular diameter 2.153 ± 0.028 mas at the parallax of Benedict et al. (2006)

mass.source: Thompson et al. (2025), AJ 170, 301, the stellar mass their orbit fit of ε Eridani b adopts, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive default parameter set

temperature.source: Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: from the interferometric angular diameter and the bolometric flux

text.card: ε Eridani is a star of 5,039 K, 3.2 parsecs away, with 1 known planet.
text.introduction: ε Eridani is a star of 5,039 K 3.2 parsecs away. Its planet is b, placed on the orbit its paper measured.
text.locator: Baines & Armstrong (2012), ApJ 744, 138, section 3: θLD 2.153 ± 0.028 mas, R 0.74 ± 0.01 solar radii, Teff 5039 ± 126 K; NASA Exoplanet Archive ps default row (THOMPSON_ET_AL_2025): st_mass 0.82

quotes.title: Epsilon Eridani
quotes.card: Epsilon Eridani, proper name Ran, is a star in the southern constellation of Eridanus.
quotes.introduction: At a declination of −9.46°, it is visible from most of Earth's surface.

notes: The star's magnetic maps (Jeffers et al. 2014, 2017, 2022) are published only as figures, so none is drawn

The planet has not been imaged: JWST/NIRCam coronagraphy found no point source (Llop-Sayson et al. 2025, arXiv:2508.08463). Earlier orbit fits put its tilt between 30 and 89 degrees; Thompson et al. (2025) measure 40 +6/-5 degrees
The spin axis is a display convention: no source used here measures its orientation

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 5164707970261890560 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
